name: struct-field
axis: struct field read/write in a tight loop — flat, then two levels of nesting
n: n=300000000 flat iterations (3 read-modify-writes each) then m=200000000 nested iterations (4 read-modify-writes through two struct levels)
notes: Every value is masked (`& 1023`, `& 63`) so the arithmetic is bit-identical in all four and Python never reaches bignum. The loop body is a serial dependency chain, so nothing vectorizes and no closed form exists; scale-verified at 1.97-1.99x for all four. Structural note: Rust SROAs a non-escaping local struct into registers, so it does no memory traffic at all — the gap to Rust here is the gap to 'no struct exists at runtime'. HEADLINE FINDING: `vl build` with no flag leaves ~3.3x on the table on this benchmark (1188ms plain vs 356ms with `-O3`), because binaryen's `--closed-world -O3 --gufa -O3` scalarizes the WasmGC struct and the default pipeline does not. `vl run main.vl` also does NOT apply it. With -O3 VL is FASTER than rustc -O here. Also carries `toplevel.vl`: byte-identical algorithm with every binding at module scope (wasm GLOBALs) instead of inside `main()` (LOCALs). MEASURED RESULT: no cliff. locals 991ms vs globals 966ms = 0.97x (min of 9, interleaved); an early sequential (non-interleaved) reading of 2.1x did not survive interleaving and was ambient load. See ../map-i32/meta.json for the scalar control probe, which also reads flat.

audit.notesClaimIsWrong: The existing note says 'The loop body is a serial dependency chain, so nothing vectorizes'. That is FALSE for the second (nested-struct) phase: disassembly of main::main shows the m-loop running paddd/pshufd/shufps 4-wide with a horizontal reduction — LLVM reassociated the masked accumulator. The first (flat) phase is correctly described (SROA'd to scalar registers, unrolled 3x, no SIMD). rustc -O 440.9ms vs -C target-cpu=native 441.3ms (a wash).
audit.protocol: ADVERSARIAL AUDIT, measurement protocol: (1) VL must be measured from a PREBUILT module — `vl run <src>` carries compile time, measured at 10-390ms (collections/map-string 1.47s prebuilt vs 1.86s from source = 27% compile; arrays/struct-aos 1.63s vs 1.92s). (2) This box swings up to 2.5x under contention even with taskset: recursion/flatcall's Rust binary read 2.53s in a sequential sweep and 0.996s as min-of-5 alone; recursion/fib's Rust read 2.02s while a second timing job ran and 0.53s alone. Every number must be min-of-N with EXCLUSIVE use of the box. (3) The known top-level-binding globals cliff is largely GONE at HEAD (#1321): measured locals-vs-globals 1.00-1.63x (f64-accum 1.63x and i64-accum 1.43x are the only real ones; fill-sum 1.05x, reverse-inplace 1.00x, map-i32 1.17x, struct-field 0.99x, char-scan 1.08x, token-count 0.95x). flatcall/flatcall-inlined/treewalk/ackermann/deeprec/mutual/tailcall spell their hot loop at TOP LEVEL while arith/* and collections/* wrap it in `function main()`; verified this no longer biases them (flatcall top-level 1.477s vs in-a-function 1.470s).
